rationale: The question is which factors go with attendance among women referred in one year, measured once for each woman: a cross-sectional study. Recorded factors and attendance come from the booking records for all 1,112 referrals; reported barriers come from a translated postal and online survey; answers are linked to attendance for women who agree. A records review alone cannot see barriers (claim c2) and a survey alone describes mostly attenders (claim c5).
alternatives: Retrospective records review only (refused as the whole study: records hold no barriers)
Qualitative interviews with non-attenders (deferred: useful after the survey shows which barriers matter most)
Before-after evaluation of evening classes (deferred: needs the survey's findings to choose the change)
guidelines: CHERRIES for the online survey mode
whyNotMoreComplex: A prospective study following new referrals would add months without changing the associations the redesign needs; one referral year answers the question.

decision.statement: Run a cross-sectional study of all women referred between September 2025 and August 2026, combining booking records for everyone with a translated barrier survey linked to attendance for women who consent.
decision.question: Should the service run a linked records and survey study of attendance before redesigning its classes?

criteria.text: Recorded factors and reported barriers each explain part of non-attendance in comparable services.
The ethics board refuses linkage of survey answers to attendance records.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board decision on a survey of referred women including non-attenders, and on linking answers to attendance records
Funding for survey printing and postage
gates.evidence: Budget line WHP-26-09 for up to 1,500, approved by the service manager and supplied by the investigator

decision.note: The survey is low risk, so the ethics decision should be straightforward.

summary: Cross-sectional linked study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims.
